questions.q: A DRAM cell with Cs = 12 fF shares charge with a bit line of Cbl = 36 fF precharged to VDD/2 = 0.55 V. Roughly what signal reaches the sense amplifier, and why can't the capacitor simply shrink with the cell footprint?
options: ~ 550 mV; it can shrink, because the sense amplifier is differential
~ 1.1 V; the word-line boost voltage VPP restores the full signal
~ 12 mV; DRAM works because reads are repeated 64 times per refresh cycle
~ 140 mV; below ~ 60-80 mV the sense amp's offset and bit-line noise cause read errors, so Cs must stay ~ 10-20 fF and the capacitor grows taller instead
questions.explanation: Charge sharing gives ΔV = 0.55 V × 12/(12+36) ≈ 140 mV. Sense amplifiers need a margin above their mismatch offset and coupling noise, so capacitance has been held roughly constant since the mid-2000s while the capacitor's height rose to > 1 µm at aspect ratios above 40.

questions.q: In the 3D NAND gate-replacement flow, when is the tungsten word-line metal actually deposited?
options: First, as alternating W/oxide layers, before the channel holes are etched
Immediately after the channel-hole etch, before the ONO and polysilicon channel

After the channel, staircase and slit are formed: hot phosphoric acid dissolves the sacrificial silicon nitride layers through the slit, and W (with TiN/Al2O3 liners) is ALD/CVD-filled into the resulting horizontal cavities
During BEOL, together with the copper bit lines
questions.explanation: The stack is deposited as oxide/nitride pairs because nitride can be etched with > 100:1 selectivity in hot H3PO4 and the etch must happen after the channel pillars exist to hold the oxide shelves up; W is then filled from the slit inward and etched back in the slit to separate the layers.

questions.q: Why does HBM4 at its JEDEC base rate deliver ~ 2 TB/s per stack while running each pin at a lower speed (~ 8 Gbps) than HBM3E (~ 9.2 Gbps)?
options: HBM4 core dies use a faster 1γ DRAM cell with lower latency
HBM4 doubles the interface from 1,024 to 2,048 data bits, so 2,048 × 8 Gbps / 8 ≈ 2.05 TB/s; bandwidth is pins × data rate
HBM4 uses hybrid bonding, which removes the solder joint resistance that limited HBM3E
HBM4 stacks are 16-high, and bandwidth scales with the number of core dies
questions.explanation: HBM is a wide-and-slow interface. HBM3E: 1,024 × 9.2 Gbps ≈ 1.18 TB/s. HBM4: 2,048 × 8 Gbps ≈ 2.05 TB/s. Doubling the width puts the burden on the base die (now made on a foundry logic process) and the interposer routing rather than on per-pin signalling.

questions.q: SK hynix's MR-MUF process won most of NVIDIA's HBM3/HBM3E business over Samsung's TC-NCF. Which statement best describes the mechanism behind that advantage?
options: MR-MUF forms all solder joints at once in a reflow oven and then injects a filled epoxy molding compound with ~ 2× the thermal conductivity of NCF, giving higher throughput, less force on thin dies, lower warpage and cooler stacks; TC-NCF bonds each die serially under heat and force through a low-conductivity film
MR-MUF uses hybrid Cu-Cu bonding with no bumps, giving a thinner stack
MR-MUF places the base die on a TSMC logic process, which Samsung could not access
MR-MUF thins dies to 30 µm, whereas TC-NCF cannot go below 100 µm
questions.explanation: Thermo-compression bonding dwells each of 12 dies at ~ 250-300 °C under force, with an epoxy film of plastic-like conductivity; mass reflow plus molded underfill parallelizes the joint formation and uses a silica-filled EMC that conducts heat better and holds the stack flatter. Samsung's 12-high HBM3E only passed NVIDIA qualification in September 2025.

questions.q: JEDEC's HBM4 standard sets the package height at 775 µm for both 12-high and 16-high stacks. What did that decision do to the technology roadmap?
options: It forced immediate adoption of hybrid bonding, because 16 microbumped dies cannot fit
It allowed 16-high stacks to be built with existing microbump TCB/MR-MUF processes by thinning core dies to ~ 30 µm, postponing hybrid bonding to HBM4E/HBM5
It made 16-high stacks impossible until 3D DRAM is available
It had no effect, because HBM height is set by the GPU lid, not by JEDEC
questions.explanation: 16 × ~ 30 µm dies + 16 bump gaps of ~ 12 µm + a ~ 50 µm base die + ~ 30 µm of bottom solder is ~ 750 µm, which fits in 775 µm with microbumps with only ~ 25 µm to spare; hybrid bonding would remove ~ 190 µm of gaps but requires sub-nm surface finishes and sub-µm placement that were not production-ready. The relaxed height therefore let vendors ship HBM4 with proven bonding.

questions.q: HBM requires 2.5 times as many wafer starts per shipped bit as conventional DRAM in an illustrative model. If 100,000 existing monthly starts are redirected from DRAM to HBM, what is the correct comparison?
options: 250,000 physical DRAM wafer starts disappear
The redirected wafers produce HBM bits equivalent to about 40,000 conventional-DRAM wafers; total bit output falls by about 60,000 conventional-wafer-equivalents
HBM bit output is 250,000 conventional-wafer-equivalents
No bit output changes because a wafer always holds the same number of useful bits
questions.explanation: 100,000 / 2.5 = 40,000. The previous 100,000-wafer conventional output is displaced, so the net total-bit reduction is 60,000 equivalents. The inverse calculation—250,000 starts—applies to producing an HBM bit quantity equal to 100,000 conventional wafers.

questions.q: Why does activating a DRAM row require restoring the stored values as part of sensing?
options: DRAM reads use ultraviolet light that destroys the oxide
Connecting a cell capacitor to the bit line redistributes its small charge; the sense amplifier resolves and restores the value
The capacitor is deliberately erased to implement wear leveling
Refresh applies only to flash, so no restoration occurs
questions.explanation: Charge sharing produces the small differential voltage used for sensing. The sense amplifier drives the selected cell back toward a clear stored state; the external read does not discard the data.

questions.q: Two 3D NAND products advertise the same layer count. Why might they still have different usable bits per square millimeter?
options: Only the product name determines density
Channel pitch, active versus support layers, bits per cell, periphery and redundancy can differ
All NAND cell areas are identical by JEDEC rule
Die area depends only on the number of packaging bumps
questions.explanation: Layer count alone omits lateral geometry, state count and overhead. Compare like-for-like active layers and complete die area, then account for usable capacity and yield.
